meta_corrections: 2026-06-30: Every full-suite test run before this correction was launched as `pytest tests/ -q 2>&1 | tail -20`, which silently truncated the FAILED-test list to whatever fit in the last 20 lines before the summary line. This session repeatedly reported '29 pre-existing failures, identical list, no regressions' across Phase 0/1/2/3a -- that claim was only ever checked against ~19-20 of the real 30 failures, never the complete set. A full untruncated run (grep '^FAILED' on raw output, no tail) found: (1) test_public_api_snapshot_v034.py was failing because of MY OWN Phase 3a change (4 new __all__ names not reflected in the frozen snapshot) -- a real regression I introduced and missed, now fixed by regenerating the snapshot; (2) 3 more call sites of the removed default_spectrolaminar_config function (test_etude1_agsdr_convergence.py, and critically the published tutorial notebook etudes/jaxfne_etude_no_1_base.ipynb) that were never previously identified; (3) 2 unrelated test_neuronal_tensor.py failures from a second consequence of the same archival (legacy-schema JSON in a directory a test assumed was tensor-only); (4) 1 fully unrelated pre-existing hygiene-check failure. Lesson: never pipe a verification run through `tail`/`head` when the claim being made is about completeness of a list -- truncation silently turns 'no regressions found' into 'no regressions found in the last 20 lines', which is a materially different and weaker claim. CONFIRMED FIXED 2026-06-30: a second complete run after the fix shows 29 failures (was 30), exact same remaining list as documented in entries[] -- regeneration worked, nothing else regressed.

2026-07-05: The 'pre-existing local kaleido-not-installed gap' cited in several commit messages/entries this session (test_vis_smoke_all.py::test_vis_smoke[exporters.export_figures]) is NOT a missing dependency -- it is an interpreter-selection artifact on this machine. `python` resolves to /opt/homebrew/bin/python (Python 3.14, no kaleido installed); `python3` resolves to /usr/local/bin/python3 (Python 3.13, kaleido 1.3.0 installed) -- both have jaxfne installed (editable), so both otherwise run the suite identically. Verified: `python -m pytest tests/test_vis_smoke_all.py -k exporters -q` -> 1 failed (kaleido ValueError); `python3 -m pytest tests/test_vis_smoke_all.py -q` -> 70 passed, 0 failed. Prior commits describing this as an unrelated pre-existing gap were accurate in the sense that it wasn't a regression from those changes, but imprecise about the cause -- it is fully avoidable by invoking `python3` (or any interpreter with kaleido installed) rather than `python`. Do not re-describe this as a missing-package gap in future entries; name the interpreter mismatch instead.

warnings: rest of file (conductivity validators, calibration/gauge/boundary, basis-spec/claim-gate) reads clean; did not exhaustively re-derive every Poisson-admissibility formula given time budget

CompilationRegistry.track_trace counts Python executions of the wrapped function's body, which only equals genuine XLA trace/compile events when the wrapper is itself the target of jax.jit -- a design constraint, not a bug per se, now made explicit in make_recompilation_guard's docstring.
entries.evidence: python3 -c 'import jaxfne.validation' succeeded; confirmed 7 underscore-prefixed jaxfne.core imports all resolve live. CORRECTED 2026-07-05 (this is why the review pass matters): the prior entry's 'REAL BUG' framing and its own reproduction called make_recompilation_guard's output DIRECTLY, bypassing jax.jit -- that is real misuse-triggered behavior, but re-verified against the ACTUAL usage pattern: grepped every one of the 5 call sites in jaxfne/_model.py (lines ~431, 531, 582, 624, 937) and confirmed all 5 immediately wrap the guard's output with jax.jit(...) before ever calling it. Live reproduction of the REAL pattern: `jax.jit(make_recompilation_guard(fn, ...))` called 3 times with an identical shape -> compilation_registry.traced_signatures shows count=1, zero warnings raised (JAX's own internal cache prevents re-executing the traced Python body on cache-hit calls). So the false-positive scenario does NOT occur via any current call site -- it's a genuine footgun only if a future call site calls the guard's output directly without jax.jit, which none does today. FIX APPLIED (docstring only, not a mechanism rewrite -- rewriting the counting itself was assessed as unwarranted risk for a non-live issue): make_recompilation_guard's docstring now states this constraint explicitly so a future call site can't skip it by accident. `pytest tests/test_v0320_recompilation_guards.py -q` -> 3 passed, ruff --select F821 clean.

entries.purpose: First CPU smoke-test implementation of the V1-PFC continuous AAAB local-oddball adaptation paradigm (0.4.6 milestone). Builds a 100n V1 + 100n PFC NeuronalTensor with a feedforward AreaConnection, both HDP-enabled, drives V1's tuning-group neurons with true 40Hz sinusoidal current in a fixed 1000ms AAAB trial, and carries HDP state trial-to-trial.
warnings: AreaConnection/InterConnection PlasticParams.H defaults to 0.0 (outside valid HDP range 0.1-10.0); construct_neuronal_tensor averages it into the target neuron's initial HDP state, so an unset H silently seeds H0 out of range and can NaN HDP integration at step 0. Always set plastic=PlasticParams(H=1.0) when HDP will be enabled.
entries.evidence: Real 10-trial CPU run (default carry_weights=False, DEFAULT_HDP_DESYNC + BASE + cube-law size scale, K_HDP=0.003): ~26s, H_final_mean converges 1.048->1.063 with H_final_std SHRINKING 0.0083->0.0031 (homeostatic settling, not divergence), rate steady ~12.9Hz, no NaN. || SUPERSEDED 2026-07-04 by the K_w_ctrl fix: the previously-recorded 'unbounded positive-feedback runaway' finding for carry_weights=True is RESOLVED, not just documented. carry_weights now defaults to True and is stable at 20 chained trials. || 2026-07-05: build_hdp_params() promoted to a thin delegate calling jaxfne.hdp_network.v1_pfc_aaab_hdp_params() (verified byte-identical output). tuning_group_indices() confirmed already a documented, real helper function -- explicit decision: sufficient as-is, no second caller to justify further promotion. || REAL 100-TRIAL RUN 2026-07-05 (closes the midterm-plan step 2 DoD's scale requirement): `run_smoke_test(n_trials=100, seed=0, carry_weights=True)` -> wall time 228.93s. Genuinely stable across the full 100 trials, not just the first/last: spike_rate_hz_mean held at 12.53-12.55Hz the entire run (trial 1 == trial 100 == 12.53Hz); w_final_mean held at 0.012248-0.012254 across all 100 trials (range of 6e-6, i.e. essentially flat, not runaway); H_final_mean converged 1.027->1.067 with H_final_std tightening 0.0201->0.0034 (homeostatic settling); zero NaN anywhere in any of the 100 trial summaries. Receipt: outputs/v1_pfc_continuous_aaab_smoke_test/100trial_receipt.json (gitignored, not tracked in git per this repo's outputs/ convention -- this evidence field is the durable record).
